text: FCY standing rule R7 (from the company corpus) — every counterparty identified with an LEI; no free-text counterparty names. This register is where that LEI lives.

comments.text: The Dependencies section cites standing rule R7 ("every counterparty identified with an LEI"), but the spec's own rules make the LEI optional: P2 says "An LEI, where present…" and nothing requires one. As written, a user can save a legal entity with no LEI at all and the register still satisfies P1–P3. If R7 is meant to bind here, there is a missing requirement (e.g. "a legal entity carries an LEI"), and A2's rejection path would need a sibling criterion for the missing-LEI case. If it is deliberately optional — perhaps because FCY's own two entities are not counterparties, or because the counterparty/Party distinction lands in the later Party spec — a sentence saying so would close the gap between the dependency and the rules. Which is intended?
